raw.assessment: The incumbent retains reversible partitions and order variants, but observed median time is 11 minutes and only seven of ten participants arranged their order unaided. Five reported partition problems warrant inspection; they do not establish five verified packing omissions. D2-O6 is a concrete limiting observation: both workers achieved seven to nine minutes on repeated three-compartment orders, so assembly is not uniformly slow. Mixed batches contain the long tail, but layout complexity and switching remain confounded. D2-O5 also limits a width-only explanation: overlapping measurements do not exclude width effects, but provide no separating threshold. Neither proposed explanation is established by these synthetic observations.

openings.claim: Switching between layouts may increase selection/checking time and component errors enough to explain some mixed-batch delays.
openings.delta: Distinguish switching overhead from intrinsically slower complex layouts before changing the assembly process.
openings.prediction: For the same layouts and colors, orders following a layout change show longer selection/checking times or more independently detected component discrepancies than repeated orders; insertion time need not differ.
openings.probe: Using reusable sample sets, have both workers complete matched blocked and interleaved sequences; counterbalance sequence order. Record selection, insertion, checking and packing separately, and independently verify contents. Compare within layout and worker. Keep accepted orders outside the trial.
assumptions: Sample reuse does not materially change fit; record wear.
The small trial fits spare-board, spending and pre-delivery labor limits; reduced switching remains a hypothesis until measured.

openings.claim: The generic three-layout diagram may leave the short partition's intended position ambiguous even when all correct parts are present.
openings.delta: Test interpretation independently of kit completeness.
openings.prediction: With independently verified identical kits, an order-specific diagram produces fewer short-partition placement errors or requests for help than the generic diagram.
openings.probe: Assign ten participants to comparable five-person groups using generic or order-specific diagrams. Record first placement, help requests and final arrangement. Treat results as preliminary; verify replacement-diagram cost before adoption.
assumptions: The diagram accurately depicts the selected arrangement and unchanged parts.
A small sample can guide further testing but cannot establish the pilot success thresholds.

raw.assessment: The observations establish packing errors, customer placement confusion and variable combined work time, but do not identify their causes. One speculative capability merits a bounded test; its cost and delivery feasibility remain unverified.

openings.claim: A removable, order-specific assembly mask could let the same physical reference guide workshop checking and customer reconstruction. Laid over the existing base, it would show each required partition's position, orientation and identity; a corresponding inventory outline would expose absent or mismatched pieces before packing.
openings.delta: Make the ordered arrangement a transferable physical reference instead of requiring both workers and customers to translate a generic three-layout diagram. The full capability depends on a verified parts list for every accepted layout, unambiguous correspondence between parts and outlines, registration to the base, usable instructions, and affordable production. The presently testable partial capability is a hand-drawn removable paper mask plus inventory outline, without changing cutting templates or shipping an unvalidated redesign.
openings.prediction: If translating the ordered layout contributes to failures, the mask should reduce short-partition placement errors and requests for help. Inventory outlines should improve detection of deliberately omitted or substituted sample pieces. These effects need not reduce insertion time.
openings.probe: Use 12 sample organizers in six matched workshop comparisons across all three compartment counts, counterbalancing mask/control order within mixed batches. Include selected-color checks and controlled missing/wrong-piece sample trials; restore complete contents before customer use. Record selection, insertion, checking, mask preparation and packing time separately. Randomly give five customers complete mask-equipped samples and five comparable controls, recording unaided ordered-layout completion and short-partition errors. These small tests screen mechanisms, not pilot success. Measure setup and recurring costs and deadline impact before adoption; any pilot must still meet the stipulated completeness, eight-minute median and customer-success thresholds.
assumptions: Existing parts can be distinguished reliably using outlines or positional drawings.
The mask removes cleanly and preserves the footprint, stationery capacity, reversible partitions, ordered counts and colors.
Preparation fits the fixed delivery schedule, initial spending stays within 500, and added material cost stays within 0.40 per order.

openings.claim: Switching may increase selection/checking time and errors.
openings.discriminator: Interleaving worsens these within layout/color/worker, without necessarily slowing insertion.
openings.probe: Counterbalance blocked/interleaved reusable samples for both workers; time four phases, verify contents, track wear; exclude accepted orders.
openings.uncertainty: Complexity confounds switching; repeats already take 7–9 minutes.

openings.claim: Generic diagrams may obscure short-partition placement.
openings.discriminator: Order-specific diagrams reduce confusion with identical verified kits.
openings.probe: Compare two comparable five-person groups; record first placement, help, final arrangement; price diagrams.
openings.uncertainty: Ten participants screen interpretation, not pilot success.

openings.claim: Removable masks transfer positional guidance; inventory outlines separately expose missing/wrong pieces.
openings.discriminator: Placement and discrepancy detection improve independently of insertion speed.
openings.fit: Uncertain registration, removal, costs and schedule.
openings.probe: Hand-draw masks/outlines: 12 samples, six counterbalanced mixed-batch comparisons across counts/colors. Seed discrepancies; restore completeness. Time four phases plus preparation. Randomize customers 5/5; record completion/errors; measure costs/deadline impact.
openings.uncertainty: Needs verified parts lists, distinguishable parts, correspondence and usable instructions; benefits unproven.

post_distill.decision: Screen D1 first; choose D2 or D3 within ten participants. Respect 15 samples, two workers/one bench, 500 initial/+0.40 per order; preserve 30×20 footprint/capacity, reversibility, counts/colors/deadline. Complaints do not establish packing omissions; width overlap supplies no threshold. Synthetic screens cannot establish pilot targets: 60 units, ≥98% complete, median ≤8 minutes, ≥90% unaided.
